column8: In Khan Younis, amid intensive military operations, the Israeli military has forced hospital staff and wounded patients to evacuate Al-Amal Hospital using smoke bombs, they have also closed the hospital gate and block roads with dirt barriers, according to the Palestine Red Crescent Society (PRCS). Starting on the night of 24 March, staff and patients were stuck in ambulances outside the hospital for 20 hours due to the damage to roads around the hospital and dirt barriers that the IDF built. When two individuals tried to move debris from the road they were fired at by IDF soldiers (PRCS on X). On 25 March, PRCS, the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), and OCHA evacuated six patients and a companion, 27 staff, and retrieved the bodies of two people who were killed inside the hospital, including a PRCS volunteer who was a member of the Emergency Operations Room. As of 26 March, both the hospital and the nearby PRCS headquarters have ceased functioning. On the same day, IFRC issued a statement, emphasizing that sustained hostilities in and around Al-Amal Hospital for over 40 days have placed PRCS teams and patients in grave danger, and that the “forced closure of Al-Amal Hospital, one of the few remaining medical facilities in the south [and the second PRCS hospital to shut down], has profound implications, leaving countless lives at risk.” [OCHA Flash Update #147]

PRCS also reported that dozens of residential buildings and people gathered at the entrance of Al-Amal Hospital had been hit, resulting in dozens more deaths and injuries [OCHA Flash Update #84]. In addition, the shelling resulted in the destruction of the transmitter station of the PRCS communications VHF, which is the only means of communication in the PRCS headquarters of Khan Yunis after the destruction of all means of communication in the Khan Yunis Governorate. The damage to the VHF communications system is a major obstacle to the response of ambulance crews to the wounded, the sick, and humanitarian cases [PRCS report 4 Jan 2024].

column8: On 29 May, Al Awda Hospital, the last minimally functional hospital in North Gaza, was forcibly evacuated and rendered out of service. According to the hospital’s Director, Mohammad Salha, Israeli forces “informed us that either we evacuate the hospital immediately or they will forcibly evacuate it.” Dr. Salha stated that 82 medical staff and 13 patients were forced to evacuate under extremely difficult conditions. With all roads leading to the hospital blocked or destroyed, ambulances could not reach the hospital and patients had to be carried for over 200 metres before reaching MoH ambulances that transferred them to Al Shifa Hospital in Gaza city, he added. Between 15 and 23 May, the hospital was repeatedly hit and faced critical shortages of medicines. On 24 and 27 May, the World Health Organization (WHO) managed to reach the facility and transferred critical patients to Al Shifa Hospital in Gaza city.

column9: Access to critical health services continues to shrink as additional evacuation orders are issued and military operations intensify in areas where these services are found. On 14 May, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) announced that it had withdrawn from the Indonesian Field Hospital after providing post-operative care for injured patients at the facility since December 2023. The NGO reported taking this decision following the “advancing offensive” in Rafah and the “pattern of systematic attacks against medical facilities and civilian infrastructure” it had witnessed since the beginning of the conflict, adding that its teams have endured 26 violent incidents since October 2023, including “airstrikes damaging hospitals, tanks being fired at agreed deconflicted shelters, ground offensives into medical centres, and convoys fired upon.” While downsizing its footprint in Rafah, MSF has now resumed operations at the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, providing orthopaedical surgery and care for burns, among other services.

column9: On 18 and 19 October, Israeli strikes reportedly impacted all three remaining hospitals in the North Gaza governorate – Kamal Adwan, Indonesian and Al-Awda. According to MoH, the top floors and front yard of the Indonesian Hospital, which hosted more than 40 trauma and chronic patients as well as medical staff, were hit and had a total power outage. Two critical patients subsequently died amid lack of electricity and supplies, MoH added. Al-Awda Hospital and the entrance to the laboratory of Kamal Adwan were also hit, resulting in casualties, Al-Awda Health and Community Association and MoH reported. On 21 October, a complex mission led by the World Health Organization (WHO), together with OCHA, the United Nations Mine Action Service (UNMAS) and the Palestine Red Crescent Society (PRCS), managed to evacuate 14 critical patients, alongside 10 caregivers, from Kamal Adwan to Al Shifa Hospital in the Gaza governorate. The mission, which departed from Deir al Balah on 20 October, had to spend the night at the Kamal Adwan Hospital due to intense fighting in the area and was only able to proceed to Al Shifa the following day. Overall, as of 21 October, 100 in-patients remained hospitalized at Kamal Adwan, including seven adults and seven children in the Intensive Care Unit, with a constant influx of new casualties flooding the emergency department; some 200 trauma patients arrived in the space of 24 hours between 20 and 21 October, including 53 already deceased. On 21 October, the Director of Kamal Adwan reported that blood units had been exhausted, medical crews have been working restlessly without food, a number of patients had succumbed to their wounds amid capacity constraints, and other wounded persons were lying in the streets with no possibility to rescue them. Meanwhile, communication challenges caused by internet outages are hampering efforts to ascertain conditions at the Indonesian and Al Awda hospitals, informs the Health Cluster. Moreover, no UNRWA medical points are currently operational in North Gaza.

column8: Between 15 and 23 May, Al-Awda Hospital, in North Gaza, was repeatedly hit. After both the Indonesian and Kamal Adwan hospitals went out of service, Al Awda became the only hospital in the governorate that remains partially functional, albeit under extreme conditions. Since 19 May, ongoing hostilities and precarious road access have prevented patients from reaching the hospital. On 21 May, the hospital’s third floor was reportedly hit, injuring a staff member. Hostilities in the area also damaged the hospital’s water tank and pipeline. On 22 May, the hospital’s third and fourth floors were reportedly hit, injuring two health workers. Al Awda faces an imminent risk of closure due to ongoing insecurity and restricted access, according to WHO.

One the 5th of February, video footage from the Hospital shows smoke dissipating from what seems to be the aftermath of a strike in the Hospital vicinity.
On February 6, the MoH made an official statement declaring that the siege imposed on the Hospital put the lifes of 300 medical staff, 450 injured, and arround 10000 IDPs at risk. With no food entering the Hospital, and no medicine and no analgesis, anesthetics, or medical surgeries equipments.
As the siege continued, allegations of Israeli snipers targeting people in the Hospital and its vacinity became numerous. On the 7th of February, a Palestinian woman was reportedly shot and killed while purpotedly fetchning water from the Hospital, And on the next day February 8, a nurse was reportedly shot and critically ijured while inside the operations room in the Hospital, in addition of two incidents where Israeli forces fired at a group of people at the entrance of the Hospital and another group in its vicinity, killing four and three Palestinians repectively.
On February 9, the Israeli snipers continue to target civilians near the Hospital with two Palestinians killed near the facility. All while the vicinity of the Hospital is repeatdly hit with strikes from the IDF. 
On the 10th February, the MoH reported continuous sniper fire targeting medical staff and IDPs taking refuge inside the Hospital, the targeting included the Hospital's entrance, its different structures and its courtyards, this has led to the death of four Palestinians.
On the same day, video footage from the within the Hospital shows and IDF armored vehicle and a Bulddozer positionned in the Hospital's gate. 
In February 11, two Palestinians were reportedly shot and killed in front of the gate of the Hospital, one of them is the journalist yasser mamdouh, Meanwhile, OCHA report that several fatalities have been lying on the ground around the hospital, for several days, and have been unreachable due to continued attacks in the Hospital's vicinity. On the same day, a video footage from within the Hospital shows two Palestinians bodies with the captions reading "Martyr's bodies that the IDF executed in front of the Hospital's entrance and prohibited medical staff from reaching them", the video shows cats feeding on the bodies. On the same day, a video footage from within the Hospital shows the aftermath of a strike that targeted the medical staff romm that served as a dorm room.
On February 12, the MoH reported seven Palestinians killed and fourteen injured by sniper fire in the Hospital's courtyard. The same authority also declared that the medical staff, the hospitalized, and the IDPs have run out of food.
In February 13, the MoH declared that the IDF have ordered the evacuation of all the IDPs from the Hospital, also reporting that the targeting of schools nearby and them catching fire have led to the burning of the Hospital's medical equipments storage room completely. MSF reported that the medical staff and patients were told they may remain with a limit of one caretaker per patient.
The IDF have desttroyed the north gate of the Hospital.
This same day saw the killing of three palestinians and the injuring of ten others inside the Hospital by sniper fire. While a generators running out of fuel and ceasing work led to the death of a ten year old child. 
 Another video footage shared by ALJAZEERA shows a Palestinian child shot by IDF snipers at the entrance of the Hospital, with his body unreachable by medcial staff being eated by cats.

column8: On 12 June, a displacement order affected the area surrounding Nasser Medical Complex, the last major functioning hospital in southern Gaza. On the same day, Medical Aid Palestine (MAP) reported that Israeli tanks and troops were in close proximity to the hospital, warning that if the hospital is forced to shut down, hundreds of thousands of people would lose access to critical care and the outcome would be “beyond catastrophic.” The hospital has 540 beds, including 51 patients in the intensive care unit (ICU), and is operating at 150 per cent of its bed capacity, MAP reported. column8: Israeli forces besieged Al-Amal hospital and the PRCS headquarters from January to March of 2024. Many sources split this siege into two seperate events, the first spanning from 22 Jan 2024, to 9 Feb 2024 when IDF forces raided the hospital, and then a second siege starting in early to mid Feb 2024 and lasting until 25 March 2024. Access to the hospital was restricted, leading to danger to patients and staff. The siege also prevented the movement of supplies into the hospital, resulting in shortages of oxygen, blood, and medical supplies as well as food, water, and fuel. By the end of the siege patients and staff were forced to evacuate the building and Al-Amal was no longer operational. PRCS reported that 27 individuals died during the siege; those individuals deaths have been recorded on the specific dates and with the specific indcidents that led to their deaths. column8: UNRWA received extremely concerning reports that Israeli Security Forces (ISF) entered one school and two health centres in Gaza city with tanks and used the installations for military operations. The reports received by UNRWA state that ISF conducted interrogations and arrests of IDPs in the installations. In one health centre, five people were reportedly killed. Witnesses reported that Israeli Forces then struck the two health centres with artillery fire. UNRWA is further verifying these reports. If confirmed, the military use of UNRWA facilities raises serious concerns, as such use puts civilians at serious risk of harm. Directing attacks against civilian objects is a serious violation of international law. Health centres, in particular, are also afforded special protection against attack.

column7: Multiple health centres froced to close due to evacuation orders and heavy fighting
column8: While health services continued, medical points in Gaza and northern Gaza were closed due to insecurity and evacuation orders and two health centres in Gaza City and northern Gaza were also closed due to heavy and continuous airstrikes in or near Jabalia camp.

column7: IDPs were forced to evacuate from a health centre
column8: On 23 October 2024, the Israeli Forces reportedly forcefully evacuated IDPs sheltering inside an UNRWA health centre and an UNRWA school in Jabalia towards West Gaza City and the south of the Gaza Strip.

column7: Image showing Israeli soldier and tank outside UNRWA Rafah health centre, with damage to the building. A video posted a few days later shows IDF soldeirs on the roof of the health centre videoing demolition of surrounding neighborhood
column8: On 5 November 2024, an image was published online displaying Israeli Forces tanks and a soldier inside the grounds of UNRWA Rafah Health Centre in Rafah. The image shows damage to this UN installation. On 8 November 2024, a video was circulated publicly displaying Israeli soldiers on the roof of the Rafah Health Centre, in Rafah Camp. An image posted in an article from +972 Magazine states that the majority of the damage done to the health centre occured on 15 July 2024, but there do not seem to be other articles or reports that confirm this.

column7: Reports that the health centre in Jabalia was severely damaged
column8: On 7 November 2024, UNRWA received reports of severe destruction of the Jabalia Health Centre that reportedly occurred in the context of the Israeli Forces military operation in Jabalia which started on 6 October 2024. A video posted online shows this UN installation burnt and severely damaged. The exact date this damage occured is not stated. Additionally, the Jabalia health centre was severely damage in July of 2024 and it is unclear what destruction was done in July and what was done in October/November.

column7: Strike in the vicinity of the health centre
column8: On 8 January, the Israeli Forces reportedly conducted a strike in the vicinity of an UNRWA health centre in Deir al-Balah Camp. It was reported that four Palestinians were killed, and others were injured outside the installation. Minor damage to the windows of the health centre was also reported.

column7: Health centre in Al Maghazi directly hit by artillery shelling
column8: On 18 January, the Israeli Forces directly struck, with an artillery shell, the third floor of an UNRWA health centre in Al Maghazi. The extent of damage to the health centre is under verification.

column7: Health centre damaged by a nearby strike
column8: On 20 March, an UNRWA health centre in Ma’an area, east of Khan Younis, reportedly sustained minor damage due to a nearby Israeli Forces airstrike. No injuries were reported.

column7: Health centre was impacted by nearby strike
column8: On 21 March, an Israeli Forces airstrike in Al Naser Area, northwest Gaza City, reportedly impacted an UNRWA health centre in Rimal, causing minor damage.

column7: First floor of Jabalia health centre struck, destroying two rooms and killing 15 people sheltering there
column8: On 2 April, the Israeli Forces hit two rooms on the first floor of an UNRWA destroyed Health Centre in Jabalia. The site was used as an UNRWA-managed shelter for 160 displaced families (or around 735 people) when it was hit. The UNRWA personnel managing the shelter did not receive any warning signals prior to the strike. Fifteen displaced people, including nine children, were reported killed in the strike. UNRWA Commissioner-General posted on X (previously known as Twitter) that “The total disregard of UN staff, premises or operations is a profound defiance of international law” and called once again for “independent investigations to find out the circumstances of each of these attacks and the serious violations.”

column7: A health centre was damaged when nearby UNRWA offices were hit
column8: On 9 May, an UNRWA Office was reportedly directly struck twice by Israeli Forces airstrikes in Jabalia, resulting in its complete destruction. Three nearby UNRWA installations – a distribution centre, a non-food items store and a health centre – sustained moderate to severe damage due to the impact of the airstrikes. No injuries were reported among UNRWA personnel.

column7: Nearby airstrike shattered the windows of a health centre
column8: On 17 May, an UNRWA health centre in Hamad City, northern Gaza, was reportedly indirectly impacted by a nearby Israeli Forces airstrike, resulting in shattered windows.

column7: Airstrike in the vicinity resulted in shattered windows
column8: On 17 May, an UNRWA training centre and a health centre in Qarrara, east Khan Younis, were reportedly indirectly impacted by an Israeli Forces airstrike and artillery shelling, resulting in shattered windows.

column7: Health centre struck by stray bullets
column8: On 4 June, two stray bullets (source of bullets unknown) struck the northeast side of the second floor of an UNRWA health centre in Khan Younis. Minor damage to the facility but no casualties among UNRWA personnel were reported.

column7: Solar panels at health centre damaged by shrapnel or bullets
column8: On 25 June 2025, two solar panels of an UNRWA health centre in Khan Younis were reportedly found damaged due to shrapnel or bullets (the source of the bullets/shrapnel is unknown).

column7: Israeli explosive caused damage to health centre in Khan Younis
column8: On 2 August, an UNRWA health centre in Khan Younis was reportedly indirectly impacted by the detonation of an explosive-laden robotic device by Israeli Forces in the nearby area. Minor damage to the facility and no casualties among UNRWA personnel were reported.

column7: Direct strikes close to a health centre led to damage
column8: Late Report: On 5 August 2025, an UNRWA health centre was reportedly impacted by an Israeli Forces airstrike at Sheikh Radwan, northeast of Gaza city, when structures close to the installation were reportedly directly struck. Significant damage to the facility and no casualties among UNRWA personnel were reported.

column7: Tank shell hit a health centre causing damage
column8: On 2 September 2025, an UNRWA health centre located in Daraj, east of Gaza City was reportedly struck by an Israeli Forces tank shell. Minor damage to the facility and no casualties among UNRWA personnel were reported.

column7: Health centre had to close after a nearby strike caused damage to the building
column8: On 12 September 2025, an UNRWA health centre was reportedly impacted due to an airstrike in Al-Nasser Neighbourhood, west of Gaza City. Significant damage to the facility and no casualties among UNRWA personnel were reported.

column7: A strike on a nearby school caused significant damage to the centre forcing it to close
column8: UNRWA was forced to suspend all health services in two facilities in Gaza City since 13 September after they sustained significant damage. This includes the suspension of activities at Beach Camp Health Centre, the only functioning UNRWA health centre north of Wadi Gaza. Previously, this facility provided health care services including outpatient care, Maternal and Child Healthcare, Physiotherapy, treatment for Non-Communicable Diseases and vaccination to over 1,000 patients on a daily basis. On 13 September 2025, an UNRWA health centre was reportedly indirectly impacted by an airstrike at the adjacent UNRWA school compound in Beach Camp, west of Gaza City. in the nearby areas in Beach Camp. Significant damage to the health facility and no casualties among UNRWA personnel were reported.

column7: UNRWA health centre gate struck by Israeli gunfire
column8: On 9 October, the northern side of an UNRWA school and the gate of an UNRWA health centre in Nuseirat were reportedly struck by Israeli forces shooting in the area. No casualties among UNRWA staff members were reported, while minor damage was reported.

column7: Gunfire in area of health centre causing damage to the structure
column8: On 9 December 2025, an UNRWA health centre in Maghazi was reportedly indirectly struck by at least two bullets due to random shooting by Israeli forces in the areas east of Eastern Maghazi, Middle Area.  No casualties among UNRWA personnel were reported, while minor damage to the facility was reported. On 13 December 2025, an UNRWA health centre in Maghazi was reportedly struck by a bullet due to an Israeli forces military operation in nearby areas, East Maghazi, South Gaza. Minor damage to the facility and no casualties among UNRWA personnel were reported. On 14 December 2025, an UNRWA health centre was reportedly struck by bullets due to Israeli forces operations in the nearby areas, East Maghazi, South Gaza. Minor damage to the facility and no casualties among UNRWA personnel were reported.

column7: Jabalia health centre was struck by tank shell
column8: On 25 January, an UNRWA Health Centre was reportedly directly struck by Israeli forces’ tank shelling in Jabalia Camp, North Gaza. Significant damage to the facility was reported, and no casualties among UNRWA personnel were recorded.

column7: Health centre struck by bullets
column8: On 30 January, an UNRWA health centre was reportedly indirectly impacted by bullets due to shooting by an Israeli forces quadcopter in Maghazi. Minor damage to the facility was reported, and no casualties among UNRWA personnel were recorded.

column7: Health centre hit by stray quadcopter fire
column8: On 24 March, an UNRWA Health Centre in Bureij, Middle Area was reportedly indirectly struck by a bullet due to nearby quadcopter fire by Israeli forces. Minor damage to the facility was reported, with no casualties among UNRWA personnel.

column7: Health centre impacted by bullets from fighting in the area
column8: On 16 April, an UNRWA health centre in Maghazi area was reportedly impacted by multiple bullets due to Israeli forces shooting in East Maghazi, Middle Area. Minor damage to the facility was reported, with no casualties among UNRWA personnel.

column7: Al Maghazi health centre was struck causing a fire
column8: On 27 December, at about 16:30, Israeli forces reportedly hit the Maghazi Health Centre, causing fire in the premises. No casualties were reported.

column7: An Israeli strike hit medicine warehouses attached to Al-Aqsa hospital. The hospital building also sustained minor damage.
column8: Israeli forces struck two medical warehouses connected to Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital, destroying the supplies stored there, including IV fluids, and materials used for dyalysis and intensive care patients
